incident-bot: [ALERT] 3191004567 - gpu-pod-restart spike on gpu-b-12 - metric: kube_pod_container_restart_total - sev=high
amanda: seeing ~18 restarts in 4m for serving-runtime pods on gpu-b-12. tagging @emily oncall.
emily: grabbing node logs and container output. first hint: dmesg showing device address translation faults and an nv driver Xid 79.
raj: runtime oncall here. if we're hitting Xid79 + device addr faults during page remap or eviction that smells like the smmu/pagewalk race we tracked before.
simon: support note: customers using embedding-api reported a wave of 5xxs around the same time. setting status to investigating.
amanda: dmesg snippet from gpu-b-12:

```
[ 45678.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:ae:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 45678.123789] kernel: device_addr_fault: 0x7f9abcd12340 (misaligned)
[ 45678.124000] nv-agent: illegal memory access from device 0000:ae:00
```

emily: container stderr shows abort due to cuda illegal memory access in loader during KV cache restore. coredump being generated to /var/tmp/incident_3191004567_core.

raj: any recent infra changes?
jess: yes — we rolled a micro-kernel tweak yesterday to change page walker ordering to mitigate a perf glitch. that patch touched SMMU PTE handling.

raj: that could be the trigger. our earlier reproductions showed unaligned device addresses appear when PTEs are swapped while long DMA (KV replay) is happening.
amanda: immediate mitigation options: cordon gpu-b-12, drain pods, migrate traffic away from nodes with the new kernel, rollback kernel tweak on canary nodes, enable CPU fallback for embedding svc.

emily: executing cordon/drain for gpu-b-12 now:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-b-12
kubectl drain gpu-b-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

deploy-bot: eviction started for pods on gpu-b-12. ETA 90s.

simon: customer comms: sending initial note that we've observed GPU node faults causing pod restarts and transient errors. traffic being re-routed; next update in 30m.

emily: drain finished but kernel oops still observed in dmesg during node cleanup. suggests kernel-level race not fully tied to workload.

jess: repro attempt plan: run KV replay loop plus aggressive unmap/evict pattern on staging with the same kernel tweak. I'll spin a staging node with the patch.

raj: please capture translator state during repro. I'll instrument runtime to print device->host translations and PTE state on failure.

emily: collection commands I'm running on node:

```
sudo journalctl -k --no-pager > /tmp/dmesg-3191004567.log
sudo /opt/nvidia/bin/nvml-snapshot --out /tmp/nvml-3191004567.json
sudo gcore -o /var/tmp/serve_core_3191004567 $(pidof serving-runtime) || true
```

infra-bot: autoscaler reported suppressed scale-up for gpu-nodegroup due to quota; eviction_count increasing.

jess: repro in staging succeeded. saw illegal memory access when KV loader replayed while we concurrently unmap a pmem-backed region. stack unwinds into runtime memcpy path referencing device pointer that appears misaligned.

raj: adding runtime instrumentation logs (excerpt):

```
[loader] translate_dev_addr(0x7f9abcd12338) -> host_phys=0x2b3c4d000 err=UNALIGNED
[loader] kv_replay chunk=105 offset=2048 -> dev_ptr=0x7f9abcd12340 (unaligned)
```

amanda: decision: roll back the kernel micro-patch from the canary pool immediately and enable CPU fallback for embedding-api for next 120 minutes. cordoned node gpu-b-12 remains isolated.

emily: rollback job queued on canary nodes in us-east-1. monitoring dmesg for new Xid79s.

deploy-bot: kernel-rollback-job-3191004567 started against pool gpu-canary. status: in_progress

simon: updated customers: we migrated traffic, initiated rollback of a recent kernel tweak that we believe is causing GPU illegal memory accesses. offered follow-up postmortem.

raj: while rollback runs, prepare a minimal kernel reproducer and open a vendor bug. include dmesg, repro harness, and coredump backtrace.
jess: will file internal ticket and vendor report with NV partner. attaching perf traces and alignment histogram showing failure bias at 8-byte offsets.

amanda: handoff: @raj owns long-term triage and vendor comms. @emily owns rollback and cluster mitigation. @simon on customer updates and postmortem. @jess will keep working on repro and test harness.

emily: rollback completed on 3 canary nodes; no new device faults observed for 12m. starting staged rollback on remaining pools. will report if faults reappear.

raj: preparing kernel bug report; provisional root cause: pagewalk/SMMU race that can leave the GPU with an unaligned device address when PTEs change under active DMA, causing immediate illegal access and container crash.

amanda: incident state: mitigating. keeping thread open until primary pool rollback completes and vendor acknowledgement. next update in 30m. :hourglass: 

simon: notes for postmortem: timeline, mitigations (cordon/drain, canary rollback, CPU fallback), customer impact (count of affected customers and failed requests), reproduction steps, and proposed long-term fixes.
